summary: Researched the evening before (Mon 16 Nov) under the stricter rules; lineups are not out, so this is a draft until the morning check and the final check. Tuesday has the last Nations League matchday for the other groups and a EuroLeague round. Ten games were researched: four are kept at medium, four at low, and two are excluded; the rest were not reached. Medium: BC Dubai v Anadolu Efes (p 0.74; Dubai at their regular home arena, Efes without Mike James, Cordinier and Bruno Fernando; Dubai miss three forwards and just lost by 29), Hapoel Tel Aviv at Baskonia (p 0.60; Baskonia are 1-11 with three injured and two new signings; Hapoel have lost three straight; the Polymarket market is thin, and bookmakers rate Hapoel higher at 71-74%), Zalgiris v Bayern (p 0.79; Zalgiris on a five-game winning streak against the league's worst defence; point guard Williams-Goss out), Hungary v Northern Ireland (p 0.46, draw 0.31, so only double chance or goals legs; Northern Ireland need just a draw to win the group and have not conceded in five games). Low, so not bet: Virtus v Panathinaikos (Panathinaikos's price fell 6.5% with no news), Barcelona v Paris (Barcelona's price fell 12% with no news, four players out), Wales v Portugal (Portugal miss Dias, Mendes, Bernardo Silva and possibly Palhinha; sources conflict), Ireland v Kosovo (no team news or lineups found). Excluded: Maccabi Tel Aviv v Olympiacos (Maccabi's home games are played in Limassol, Cyprus: neutral venue), Bosnia v Romania (Bosnia's second place is already fixed while Romania need a win to avoid the relegation play-off). Morning check (Tue): no new team news overnight. Hapoel's price rose from 62% to 77% with no news, the thin Polymarket market catching up with the bookmakers (71-74%); kept at medium. Zalgiris's price fell 3.7% since first listing with no news to explain it, so it is now low. Dubai (-2.6%, injury lists unchanged) and Hungary (price stable, same suspensions) stay medium.

checks.team_news: Unchanged from Monday night, nothing new found this morning. Zalgiris: Nigel Williams-Goss (thigh) out for both of this week's EuroLeague games per coach Tomas Masiulis (BasketNews.lt); Keenan Evans brought back as cover; no other Zalgiris absence found. Bayern: center Austin Wiley (hip) uncertain per German press but he travelled to Kaunas. Searches this morning for the Round 12 injury report, Monday press conferences and any Zalgiris or Bayern absence returned only older-season items; the official report was not readable (euroleaguebasketball.net returned 429 earlier, so not used again). No news found that explains the price fall.
checks.lineups: No official or predicted starting fives found this morning. Expected from previews (unconfirmed): Zalgiris with Evans or Jokubaitis at guard, Grigonis, Valanciunas at center; Bayern with Obst and Wiley if fit. To be checked at the final check.
checks.rotation: Unchanged: Zalgiris beat Armani Milan 86-83 away on 12/13 Nov (five-game winning streak) and had rest before Tuesday. Bayern lost 102-87 to Valencia and travelled Monday, with a Thursday home game vs Baskonia (double week); partial rotation possible but not confirmed.
checks.motivation: Zalgiris 8th at 7-4, Bayern 18th at 3-8; both need wins.
checks.form: Zalgiris 5 straight EuroLeague wins, net rating -5.1 (3StepsBasket). Bayern 3-8, three wins all away, net rating -9.9, worst defense in the league.
checks.h2h: Zalgiris won both 2025-26 meetings (98-70 in Munich, 78-71 in Kaunas per bet-experts); thetopbookies claims a different 3-2 Bayern record over five meetings, so h2h is a weak signal.
checks.odds: Polymarket home 0.785 live now vs 0.815 at first listing and last night (-3.7%, past the 3% line) and vs 0.805 24h ago (-2.5%). Away rose 0.185 to 0.215. Searches found no injury, illness, Bayern return or lineup news that explains the drop, so the fall is unexplained and confidence goes to low. Bookmaker check: bet-experts page (checked 15 Nov, no movement history) shows Zalgiris about 1.21 / Bayern about 5.75 (81% / 19%), spread -9.5 at 1.93, total 171.5; thetopbookies (1xBet 1.19 / 4.60, about 79% / 21%) returned 429 this morning so no fresh bookmaker price was seen. Bookmaker prices are older than the Polymarket move, so they cannot confirm it.
checks.models: No bookmaker-free model found. 3StepsBasket net-rating gap of about 4.8 plus about 3 points home court implies roughly an 8 point margin, a little under the -9.5 market line; this supports shading below the market, hence p home 0.77.
checks.venue_weather: Zalgirio Arena, Kaunas, genuine home game, Tue 17 Nov 18:00 UTC (20:00 local). Indoor, no weather issue.

games.reason: Zalgiris is at home on a five-game winning streak against the league's worst-defending side (3-8), and bookmaker prices from the weekend were around 79-81%. No hard exclusion applies. Confidence drops to low this morning because the Polymarket price has fallen 3.7% since first listing (0.815 to 0.785) and no news found explains it; Williams-Goss was already known to be out.
games.main_risk: Unexplained 3.7% drop in the Zalgiris price since first listing, which may reflect news or a bookmaker move I could not find; Williams-Goss is out; both teams have weak net ratings (gap about 4.8), so a close loss is plausible; Bayern's Wiley and Obst could be available; lineups and the official injury report remain unseen.

checks.team_news: Morning update (BasketNews EuroLeague injury report, stamped 16 Nov 19:54): Dubai OUT for round 12: Davis Bertans (hamstring, indefinite, missed R10-11), Mouhammadou Jaiteh (Achilles rehab, indefinite), Kosta Kondic (hip/psoas, missed R10-11); also Awudu Abass out (not on the EuroLeague roster). None of the three injured forwards is returning. Expected: Thomas Walkup (back, back in the ABA League 15 Nov) and Justin Anderson (hamstring); Marcelinho Huertas (new signing) game-time; Klemen Prepelic uncertain (coach's decision, missed R8-11). Efes: Mike James OUT FOR SEASON (Achilles surgery), Isaia Cordinier out indefinitely (post-surgery), Bruno Fernando out (calf, 3-4 weeks per club doctor/Eurohoops; BasketNews says possibly until R15-17). Nobody on the Efes absentee list is returning; fringe players Fenemen, Karutasu, Mutaf are doubtful (coach's decision). Last night's note that P.J. Dozier is returning was not seen on this report, so treat it as unconfirmed. No official EuroLeague report read (site 429 earlier, not used).
checks.lineups: No predicted XIs or starting fives found this morning for either side. Official lineups come at the final check.
checks.rotation: Unchanged: Dubai lost 101-72 at Olympiacos on 12 Nov and have 4-5 days rest at home. Efes beat Virtus 103-91 in R11 and played a domestic league game on 15 Nov (Mutaf played, Karutasu did not), then travel to Dubai. No rotation announcement found.
checks.motivation: Unchanged: Dubai 7-4 coming off a heavy loss and wanting to avoid a third home defeat; Efes 5-6 needing wins. No hard rule applies.
checks.form: Unchanged: Dubai last 5 LWWLW, 86.5 scored / 85.6 allowed; Efes last 5 WLWLW, 85.9 scored / 87.5 allowed.
checks.h2h: Unchanged: Dubai won 80-76 at Efes (19 Dec 2025); Efes won 85-69 in Sarajevo (10 Apr 2026). Split 1-1.
checks.odds: Polymarket live 0.74 Dubai (candidates file refreshed 06:51 UTC); last night 0.76, first listed 0.76, so -0.02 (-2.6% relative) overall, the whole drop came overnight; the file's own 24h move shows 0.74 to 0.74, i.e. flat in the last hours. The drift does not seem to be explained by team news: the injury lists are the same as last night and the only Dubai movements are positive (Walkup, Anderson expected). A small fade after the 29-point loss and thin frontcourt is the likeliest cause but I could not confirm that. It is under the 3% threshold, so confidence stays medium. Bookmakers this morning: could not find fresh November prices (oddspedia returned 403, searches only returned April/December 2025 pages); last night's second-source prices (1xBet 1.28/3.60, de-vigged Dubai about 0.74; BetMGM 7/20) are from Monday and agree with the live 0.74.
checks.models: Unchanged: season net ratings favour Dubai by roughly 6-7 points before home court, consistent with about 73-75%, small samples.
checks.venue_weather: Unchanged: Coca-Cola Arena, Dubai, Tue 17 Nov 20:00 local (16:00 UTC), indoor.

games.reason: Fixture and venue verified; no hard exclusion. Dubai remain favourites on home court and an Efes roster missing Mike James (out for the season), Cordinier and Fernando, while Dubai are missing Bertans, Jaiteh and Kondic with Walkup and Anderson expected back. The price slipped from 0.76 to 0.74 with no news explaining it (-2.6%, below the 3% low-confidence trigger), so p is trimmed one point under the live market.
games.main_risk: Dubai are inconsistent (lost 101-72 at Olympiacos, two home losses already) and thin up front; Efes could win a close game. The overnight drift from 0.76 to 0.74 is unexplained by news, and I found no fresh bookmaker prices this morning. A further slide before tip-off, or Walkup/Anderson being ruled out, would push confidence to low.

checks.team_news: No current injury report or press-conference news found for either side for Round 12. Search results only returned older items (e.g. Kendrick Nunn's earlier-season ailments, Richaun Holmes missing the Round 6 game at Bologna with a thigh injury, Scariolo comments from earlier seasons). Status of Nunn, Holmes and Virtus's roster for 17 Nov is unverified.

checks.form: Panathinaikos 8-2 after round 10 and won 115-112 in OT at Real Madrid (4 Nov). Full last 6-10 results with points for/against and home/away splits were not found.

That is above the 3% threshold and I found no news explaining it (no injury or lineup report surfaced). Fixture date, teams and competition (EuroLeague Round 12, Tue 17 Nov 2026) are confirmed. Not a neutral venue; indoor, weather irrelevant.

games.reason: Fixture verified and no hard exclusion found, but the favourite's Polymarket price fell 6.5% in 24h with no news found to explain it, and injury, lineup and second-bookmaker data are all missing. Honest rating is low; p shaded toward the underdog.
games.main_risk: Unexplained 6.5% drop in Panathinaikos's price (possible late absence such as Nunn or Holmes that I could not find), plus Bologna at home with a history of beating Panathinaikos (92-75 in Oct 2025).

games.reason: HARD rule: neutral/unusual venue. Maccabi's EuroLeague home games are not played in Tel Aviv. EuroLeague approved the Spyros Kyprianou Arena in Limassol, Cyprus as Maccabi's home venue until further notice, starting with Round 11 (Hapoel game on 12 Nov 2026), per Eurohoops and Cyprus Mail on 4 Nov 2026. The 17 Nov game is Round 12, so it falls under this arrangement and is a home game played abroad. The Polymarket favourite price also jumped from 0.43 to 0.695 in 24h (+61.6% relative), which I could not explain from the venue news alone.
games.main_risk: Home game played abroad in Limassol (neutral venue, no real home advantage); also an unexplained 24h price jump on Olympiacos (0.43 to 0.695).

checks.team_news: Portugal: Ruben Dias suspended (yellow vs Denmark), Joao Palhinha also reported suspended (Goal), Nuno Mendes injured, Bernardo Silva sent home as physically unfit (Goal) / a knock (Portugoal), Cancelo back from suspension. Portugal's first match since Cristiano Ronaldo's official farewell. Wales (Sports Mole, 16 Nov): Ethan Ampadu suspended, Neco Williams injured, Connor Roberts expected to replace him, David Brooks scored in Norway. Sources conflict on some Portugal absences (Palhinha is in the Portugoal predicted XI but Goal says suspended); no press conference found.
checks.lineups: Not out. Sports Mole predicted Portugal: D Costa; A Costa, A Silva, Veiga, Dalot; J Neves, Vitinha; B Silva, Felix, Fernandes; Ramos (lists B Silva although Goal says he left the camp). Portugoal predicted: D Costa, A Costa, Veiga, A Silva, Cancelo, Palhinha, B Fernandes, Vitinha, Forbs, Felix, Ramos. Sports Mole predicted Wales: Darlow; Roberts, Rodon, Davies, Dasilva; Cullen, Sheehan; Johnson, Brooks, Wilson; Koumas. Two sources disagree, so the Portugal XI is unverified.
checks.rotation: Portugal played Denmark on Sat 14 Nov (lost 1-4 at home), Wales played in Norway the same day (lost 1-3); both have 3 days' rest. Portugal travel to Cardiff. No further games before the tie-up of the group. Three or four Portugal regulars are out for reasons other than rotation (suspension, injury, fitness).
checks.motivation: Sky Sports table (updated 16 Nov 18:55), 5 played each: Portugal 12 pts (W4 L1, GF10 GA8, GD+2), Denmark 9 (GD+3), Norway 6 (GD 0), Wales 3 (GD-5). Last matchday: Wales v Portugal and Denmark v Norway on 17 Nov. Portugal cannot finish below 2nd (Denmark max 12 and Portugal already 12), but first place is NOT secured: a Portugal defeat plus a Denmark win leaves them level on 12 and Denmark won the head-to-head on aggregate (Portugal 4-2 Denmark earlier, Denmark 4-1 Portugal on 14 Nov), so Portugal need at least a draw for sure first place. Sports Mole says Portugal must avoid defeat to keep top spot. Wales are bottom with 3 pts; a win would lift them level with Norway on 6, so they still play for 3rd (relegation play-off) versus 4th (relegation); sources differ (Sports Mole: Wales need a point to secure the play-off; Portugoal: already relegated). Denmark v Norway matters: Denmark need a win and a Portugal slip for first place. Verdict: not a hard exclusion, since the favourite still needs a point; soft risk because Portugal's aim is partly secured (quarter-final place) and Wales and Denmark have more to gain.
checks.form: Portugal: five straight wins ended with the 1-4 home loss to Denmark (worst home competitive defeat per press); earlier 1-0 home win over Wales (24 Sep, Felix) and 4-2 win at Denmark. Wales: 1 win in the last 9 matches, 3-1 loss in Norway on 14 Nov (Brooks goal); Wales GF3 GA8 over 5 group games. No xG found.
checks.h2h: 24 Sep 2026 Portugal 1-0 Wales in Lisbon (Wales faced 23 shots, only a deflected Felix goal separated them). Wales are a low-scoring side so a narrow Portugal win or a draw is the main alternative path.
checks.odds: DraftKings via ESPN (data.odds): Wales 6.00, Draw 4.70, Portugal 1.42 (opening 1.40), de-vigged Wales 15.4%, draw 19.6%, Portugal 65.0%, total 3.5. Polymarket Portugal 66.5% -> 68.5% over 24h (+3% relative, a rise, so not a fall). A Wincomparator model page quotes Portugal 52.75% (commercial, unreliable). Market price of 68% is above the de-vigged 65% and above Elo (below), so p is trimmed to 65%.
checks.models: World Football Elo (eloratings.net): Portugal 1996, Wales 1673, expected score for Wales 0.217 (draw counts half), which implies roughly Portugal 66-70% before depleted-squad adjustment.
checks.venue_weather: Cardiff City Stadium, Tue 17 Nov 2026, 19:45 (Sports Mole, Kickoff.co.uk); ordinary home venue. Cardiff forecast for that evening not found (searches returned undated results), so weather is unverified; no pitch problem reported. Goal's listing shows 13:45 for the time, probably in another time zone.

games.reason: Not a hard exclusion: table checked first, Portugal (12 pts) are through to the quarter-finals but still need a point to guarantee first place over Denmark (9 pts, with the head-to-head advantage), and Wales (3 pts, bottom) still have the 3rd-versus-4th relegation stakes. Portugal also lose Dias, Mendes, Bernardo Silva and possibly Palhinha, and just conceded four at home. Confidence is low because squad and lineup facts conflict across sources and are unconfirmed, the weather is unverified and Portugal's own defeat would not cost them a quarter-final place.
games.main_risk: A draw or upset: depleted Portugal (Dias suspended, Mendes injured, Bernardo Silva out, Palhinha reported suspended) after a 1-4 home loss, against a Wales side that still plays for relegation play-off survival and held Portugal to 1-0 in September; Wales have scored 3 goals in 5 group games, so a narrow 1-0 or a 0-0/1-1 draw is the likely failure for any handicap or goals leg.

checks.team_news: Barcelona: Kevin Punter (top scorer, 15.9 ppg, ankle sprain, about 6 weeks), Tosan Evbuomwan (oblique tear, about 3 weeks), Umoja Gibson (muscle strain, about 3 weeks) and Yoan Makoundou (knee) are out; Juan Nunez (right ankle sprain) is day-to-day (basketballsphere.com EuroLeague injury page updated 16 Nov; Infobae preview 16 Nov). Paris: no injured players listed; Daulton Hommes missed rounds 9-10 and returned in the French league at the weekend. No Barcelona press-conference quote found, so Nunez's status is unconfirmed.
checks.lineups: Not out yet. Infobae (16 Nov) probable fives: Barcelona Robinson, Brizuela, Parra, Martin, Nebo (Nunez on the bench list, not a starter); Paris Hifi, Herrera, Warren, Dokossi, Faye. Only one source found for the XIs, so they are unconfirmed.
checks.rotation: Barcelona won 76-74 at Panathinaikos in round 11 (Thursday, about 4 days' rest, a Barcelona win after a 3-day trip to Athens), then host Paris on Tue 17 Nov (round 12). Paris beat Fenerbahce 111-109 in overtime on Wed 11 Nov at home and played the French league at the weekend, so they have a similar rest. The kickoff is listed as 20:30 Spanish time (19:30 UTC). I did not find either side's next fixture.
checks.motivation: EuroLeague standings after round 11 (Wikipedia, through 13 Nov): 1 Valencia 8-3, 2 Panathinaikos 8-3, 3 Olympiacos 8-3, 4 Barcelona 8-3 (+30), 5 Real Madrid 7-4 ... 12 Anadolu 5-6, 13 Besiktas 5-6, 14 Paris 5-6 (-36). Both want wins; Barcelona are in the top-4 race, Paris are chasing the play-in places. Nothing is secured, so no hard exclusion.
checks.form: Barcelona: 8-3, 978 points for, 948 against (+30); 3-2 at home; won 93-90 at Hapoel on 5 Nov and 76-74 at Panathinaikos in round 11, both close. Justin Robinson has scored 10 or more in 8 straight games. Paris: 5-6, 982 for, 1018 against (-36); four straight wins, including 95-90 at Efes and the 111-109 overtime win over Fenerbahce; Hifi leads the league in scoring (20.8 ppg) and Paris have the third-best offence (about 91 ppg).
checks.h2h: The road team won all of the last four Barcelona-Paris meetings by double digits, including Paris 85-74 at the Palau in Feb 2026 and 103-87 in Nov 2024 (Infobae preview; EuroLeague game notes). That is a poor sign for a home favourite, though the squads have changed.
checks.odds: Polymarket moneyline for Barcelona: 0.73 at 20:00 UTC on 15 Nov, 0.72 at 11:00 UTC on 16 Nov, then a drop to 0.65 at 12:00 UTC and 0.64 now (move_24h 0.73 to 0.64, -12.3% relative). I found no news that explains it: the Punter, Evbuomwan and Gibson absences were already known, so the confidence is low under the price-move rule. Other books: FanDuel (search snippet) Barcelona -380 / Paris +280, spread Barcelona -8.5, which de-vigs to about 75% / 25% for Barcelona; bet-experts quotes Barcelona about 1.34-1.37 and Paris +7.5 at 1.93. The books are well above Polymarket's 64%, and I could not tell how current the snippets are. Polymarket spread Barcelona -8.5 is priced at 0.23 and the total at 185.5 is 50/50. I did not find a Stake or Rainbet price.
checks.models: No bookmaker-free rating, such as net rating or a power ranking, was found for this season. Point difference per game from the Wikipedia table: Barcelona +2.7 (+30 over 11), Paris -3.3 (-36 over 11), a gap of about 6 points per game, plus home court for Barcelona. This points to a Barcelona edge of roughly 6-8 points, and Paris's offence is strong, so the gap is not safe.
checks.venue_weather: Palau Blaugrana, Barcelona, is Barcelona's normal home arena (indoor, no weather risk); the Barcelona home record is only 3-2.

games.reason: Barcelona are the clear on-paper favourite: the better record and point difference, at home, and the books price them at about 75%. The confidence is low because the Polymarket price dropped 12% in 24 hours (0.73 to 0.64, mostly at 12:00 UTC on 16 Nov) with no explanatory news found, because Barcelona are missing their top scorer Punter plus Gibson, Evbuomwan and Makoundou with Nunez doubtful, and because the visitor won each of the last four meetings by double digits. Paris are on a four-game winning streak. So p is trimmed below the market within 5 points.
games.main_risk: Paris keep scoring against a Barcelona side without Punter, Gibson and Evbuomwan, with Nunez doubtful, and win or keep it close; the favourite's unexplained price drop (-12% in 24h) could reflect information I did not find, such as a late injury or lineup news.

checks.team_news: Morning re-check (Tue 17 Nov): no new news found. Baskonia (1-11, last) still without Kenneth Faried, Marcio Santos and Tadas Sedekerskis; the Infobae/EFE preview of 16 Nov names the same three and says debutants Rolands Smits and Kenan Kamenjas will be fundamental. That article lists no Hapoel absences and names Bryant, Micic, Blakeney and Oturu as the key players. Earlier reports still stand: Tyler Ennis (Achilles) out, Micic had a groin problem on 9 Nov but played on 12 Nov (14 pts). Caboclo (minor calf, one tracker only) and Satoransky (missed the 9 Nov Winner Cup final) are still unconfirmed, and I could not find a Round 12 injury report. The official EuroLeague injury page returned HTTP 429, so I stopped using that site. Search results this morning mixed in other seasons and gave nothing reliable on Micic, Satoransky or Caboclo for this game, so the risk stays open until the official lineups.
checks.lineups: Not out yet. Expected Hapoel core from previews: Micic, Elijah Bryant, Antonio Blakeney, Dan Oturu. Baskonia: thin and rebuilt, with Smits and Kamenjas due to debut in the EuroLeague. No confirmed fives; official lineups are for the final check.

checks.motivation: Unchanged. Baskonia 1-11, last, in crisis and wanting a second win. Hapoel 6-5, 10th, on a 3-game losing run and fighting for the top-10 line. The nothing-to-play-for rule is not triggered. Coach Perasovic was appointed on 14 Oct (more than 7 days ago).
checks.form: Unchanged. Baskonia 0-5 in their last five and 0-5 away, margin -12.0, the worst offence in the league. Hapoel margin +3.2, 90.4 points scored, but lost 73-80 at Maccabi on 12 Nov and the Winner Cup final on 9 Nov after leading by 23.
checks.h2h: 1-1 in 2025-26: Hapoel won 114-89 in Nov 2025, Baskonia won 118-109 on 27 Mar 2026 (behind closed doors). Both high scoring. Hapoel's 2nd most turnovers and Baskonia's offensive rebounding keep an upset in play.
checks.odds: Hapoel prices: first listed 0.625, last night 0.625 (0.635 at 19:20 UTC on 16 Nov), live this morning 0.765 (+22% vs last night, +22% vs first listing; the file's own 24h move shows 0.78 to 0.765, so the price had already jumped before the morning refresh and is flat to slightly down since). I found no news that explains the jump. It fits a very thin market (about $37 traded last night, with swings from 0.435 to 0.78 on 15-16 Nov) converging to the bookmakers, who already had Hapoel at about 71-74%: FanDuel -300/+225 (de-vigged about 70.9%) and Bet-Experts 1.34/3.92 (about 74.5%). Both are last night's quotes. I could not find a fresh bookmaker price this morning (sportschedule.tv shows an undated 1.19 / 4.8 that I cannot tie to this game, so I ignore it). Live 0.765 is slightly above the 71-74.5% book range, so I set p a little under the market at 0.72, in line with the books. Spread -6.5 was priced 0.50 last night; total 181.5.
checks.models: No bookmaker-free model found. Basketballsphere season margins: Hapoel +3.2 vs Baskonia -12.0 (a 15-point gap), and its pick is Hapoel -5.5. This points to a clear but not huge Hapoel win, consistent with about 72%.
checks.venue_weather: Fernando Buesa Arena, Vitoria-Gasteiz, Tue 17 Nov, 20:30 CET (19:30 UTC), EuroLeague Round 12; Baskonia are the home side. In March the game against Hapoel in Vitoria was played behind closed doors by order of the Basque Government. I found no announcement for 17 Nov (the Infobae preview does not mention fans), so I do not know if fans are admitted. Indoor game, weather irrelevant.

games.reason: Hapoel remain a clear favourite: 6-5 and +3.2 margin against a 1-11 Baskonia at -12.0 with Faried, Santos and Sedekerskis out, the weakest offence in the league and two debutants still integrating. The overnight jump from 0.625 to 0.765 has no news behind it and looks like a thin market catching up with the bookmakers (about 71-74.5%), so it does not add information. No hard exclusion applies. p is set at 0.72, below the live market, because of the unconfirmed Micic/Satoransky/Caboclo status, Hapoel's 3-game losing run and the new-coach bounce risk.
games.main_risk: A Micic groin relapse or an absent Satoransky/Caboclo (still unconfirmed, with no official injury report found), Hapoel's three straight defeats and 2nd most turnovers, and a Baskonia side with new signings that is dangerous on offensive rebounds and could get a home bounce. Hapoel at -6.5 is priced even, so an outright win is likelier than covering. The live 0.765 comes from a market with very little volume, so it could still swing.

games.reason: Hard rule 'favourite has nothing left to play for and the opponent does'. Group B4 table before this game (5 games played): Sweden 13 (group winner, promoted), Bosnia and Herzegovina 8, Poland 4, Romania 3. Bosnia are already assured of second place and the March League A promotion playoff. Poland (4 pts, one game left, away to Sweden) can reach at most 7, so Bosnia's final position cannot change; Klix and RTV Slon say the result does not alter their placement. Romania are bottom and must win in Zenica and also need Sweden not to lose to Poland, otherwise they finish last and face the relegation playoff against a League C runner-up (Klix, Sports Mole, N1). Bosnia lost 3-2 to Sweden on 14 Nov, their first defeat of the campaign, which cost them first place. This is the Portugal-Denmark pattern: a favourite whose aim is already secured against an opponent who needs the result. Other facts: venue is Bilino Polje, Zenica (home, 20:45 local = 19:45 UTC), no venue issue. Bosnia doubts: striker Tabakovic (knee) and Hadzikadunic out. Romania are missing GK Radu, Mihaila, Stanciu and the suspended Baluta; Marin returns. Hagi's squad had 12 changes. No coach change. DraftKings home moved 1.91 to 1.83 (de-vig 50.5%); World Football Elo has Bosnia 1662 vs Romania 1576 (expected score 0.745).
games.main_risk: Bosnia have nothing to gain from the result (second place and the playoff are fixed) while Romania need a win to avoid the relegation playoff, so a draw or Romania win is more likely than the market implies. Possible Bosnia rotation, and Tabakovic and Hadzikadunic are out or doubtful.

checks.team_news: Morning re-check: Racing Post preview (updated 16 Nov 16:39) is unchanged from last night. Hungary without suspended Willi Orban and Milan Vitalis, Damir Redzic a doubt, Barany, Lukacs, Szucs and Alex Toth injured.
